_doc: Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34) — v2 RICH, context-driven scene plan. Rebalanced away from 'Jesus in various poses' (6/13 Christ-centric = 46%, PASSES render_lint.verify --plan). Red-teamed BOTH ways (doctrine + craft) 2026-07-01; both REVISE, all flags folded in below (v2.1). Render rule: christ_* subject_types lock to the Christ face ref (nail_wide_45 for passion, JESUS__REF for risen); context_scene/ot_echo/human_us/symbolic render WITHOUT the Christ ref (no face-bleed). Timeline synced to the 8 real audio turns.

candidates.concept: Macro of a single forged square iron nail driven through an open palm against dark wood
Roman soldiers crouched in the dust at the foot of a cross, casting pale pebbles and broken pottery shards over a folded garment
A shadowed crowd of onlookers with hard mouths, leaning in as if braced for a curse to fall
The face of Christ lifted on the cross, lips just parting to speak
Extreme reverent close of Christ's face, eyes lowered toward his killers, the prayer forming
An ancient hand of David the psalmist over an unrolled scroll with only vague ink marks, foretelling the parted garments
A seamless woven robe held up in one soldier's fist while pebbles fall in the dust below
The weathered face of a single executioner, unknowing, caught in the light of the one he crucifies
Ordinary bowed figures kneeling small under the long shadow of the cross falling across the dust
Christ on the cross, head bowed in willing surrender, no hand forcing him
The risen Christ standing in radiant light, one open palm showing a single healed nail-hole, raised in intercession
Darkness swallowing the land over the hill, a single shaft of light breaking the gloom
The risen Christ, healed hand extended toward the viewer in mercy, glowing warm
A great temple veil torn from top to bottom, light pouring through the rent
Isaiah standing on a windswept ridge, arm outstretched, foreshadowing the one numbered with transgressors
Wide silhouette of three crosses on a bleak hill against a bruised sky
A soldier's dust-caked hand releasing pale pebbles that scatter across a folded cloak
The risen Christ's clean open palm with one healed nail-hole, fingers unmarked
A lone kneeling figure at the base of the cross reaching up an empty hand
The scapegoat led into the wilderness, an OT shadow of sin borne away

scenes.concept: A forged square iron nail driven through an open palm against dark cross-wood.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel close-up of a single forged square iron nail through the center of an open human palm pressed to dark rough cross-wood, one dominant subject, bold black ink linework, flat cel-shaded muted crimson and grey, reverent, cinematic-manga, 1st-century, dramatic side light
scenes.why: Opens on the wound the hook names ('Nails through his hands') and plants the piercing under the very first image.

scenes.concept: Wide at the foot of the cross: the whole crucified figure above, Roman soldiers crouched below casting lots — establishes THAT this is a crucifixion.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel wide of a crucifixion on a bleak hill: the full crucified man on a tall wooden cross, head bowed, arms nailed along the beam, and at the foot two or three 1st-century Roman soldiers crouched in the dust casting a few pale rounded pebbles over a folded woven garment, one dominant grouping, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded ochre and iron-grey, reverent, dark storm sky, period-accurate
scenes.why: Fixes the under-shown-cross flag: establishes the crucifixion clearly by ~4s, AND carries 'soldiers at his feet, gambling for his clothes'.

scenes.concept: A shadowed crowd mocking — shaking heads, shot-out lips — the scorn a curse was expected to answer.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of a 1st-century crowd mocking, with only THREE distinct foreground mockers, each a clearly DIFFERENT person — a grizzled grey-bearded old elder, a younger clean-shaven man, and a heavy middle-aged man with a dark beard — jeering upward with open scornful mouths and pointing hands, in dusty earth-toned head-wraps and coarse tunics; behind them the rest of the crowd is a DARK FEATURELESS SILHOUETTE MASS with no individual faces, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded dusk palette, reverent tone despite the scorn, tension
scenes.why: Grounds Ps 22:7 in the actual mockery (not an invented 'curse-bracing'); sets up 'a word no one expected — not a curse' by showing the scorn a curse would have answered.

scenes.concept: Christ's face and shoulders on the cross, arms along the crossbeam, lips just parting to speak instead of curse.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of the face, shoulders and outstretched arms of the crucified Christ on the wooden crossbeam, eyes lowered with compassion, lips just parting to speak, one dominant subject, bold black ink linework, flat cel-shaded warm skin against a dim storm sky, reverent, cinematic, 1st-century, soft rim light
scenes.why: The turn: the crowd expected a curse; we cut to the mouth about to pray. Widened to face+shoulders+arms so the cross clearly reads. No crown of thorns (matches the locked look).

scenes.concept: Extreme reverent close of Christ's praying face — the red-letter 'Father, forgive them' anchor.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel intimate close of the crucified Christ's face in prayer, eyes lifting past the frame toward the light, brow easing, one dominant subject, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded warm tones, reverent, cinematic-manga, negative space above for later caption furniture
scenes.why: The essential red-letter prayer anchor; held to the full prayer window (16.94-22.06) so it does not cut away before 'they know not what they do' ends. No thorns. PIL red-letter bar sits in the negative space above.

scenes.concept: David the psalmist's hand over an ancient scroll, foretelling the parted garments a thousand years early.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of an aged hand of an ancient Hebrew psalmist resting on a half-unrolled scroll seen at a steep raking side-angle so the parchment is strongly foreshortened and its writing reads only as faint indistinct rhythmic horizontal ink strokes with no separate letters and no alphabet; a young white lamb lying quietly in FRONT of the scroll as the clear focal subject (the foreshadowed sacrifice), a small clay oil lamp casting warm amber light, one dominant subject, bold black ink of the SAME line-weight and reverence as the Golgotha scenes, flat cel-shaded amber lamplight, reverent, 1st-millennium-BC
scenes.why: The OT-echo, placed under 'Luke records it as they gambled:' — the SETUP: the soldiers' lots fulfill Psalm 22:18 written ~1000 years before. Christ absent — the shadow speaking. Illegible marks avoid the animate-writing trap; keep ink identical so it reads as the same world's memory.

scenes.concept: A soldier lifts the seamless robe as the lots fall — the prophecy fulfilled in real time.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of a seamless woven robe held up in one Roman soldier's hand while two or three clearly-thrown pale lots land in the dust below, the gambling read unmistakable through the soldiers' intent crouch, one dominant subject, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded ochre and grey, reverent, low angle, 1st-century
scenes.why: Now synced ON the [scripture] line 'And they parted his raiment, and cast lots' (24.22-26.78) — the visible fulfillment of the scroll we just saw. Lots read as gambling via body language, not dice.
scenes.reuse: reshoot 04 (re-render to land on the words)

scenes.concept: A single executioner mid-deed — hand still on the mallet — hard-faced and unknowing: the guilty sinner he intercedes FOR.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel close of a single weathered 1st-century Roman executioner still at his work, one hand gripping a heavy iron mallet, brow furrowed in hard duty, unaware of who he kills, ordinary grey daylight (not glorified light), one dominant subject, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded dusty tones, reverent, cinematic
scenes.why: Gives a face to 'they know not what they do' AND 'intercedes for the sinner' — but keeps him CULPABLE (mid-deed, plain daylight), not a sympathetic innocent bathed in mercy-light, so it does not soften guilt the narration forbids excusing.

scenes.concept: Ordinary bowed figures kneeling small under the long cross-shadow — the sin was ours too.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of two or three ordinary bowed figures kneeling small in the dust as the long shadow of a cross falls across them, one dominant grouping, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded muted earth tones, reverent, wide, the cross implied only by its shadow
scenes.why: Turns the accusation inward — 'the sin that put him there was ours too' — placing the viewer under the shadow, not another Christ figure.

scenes.concept: Christ on the cross, head bowed in willing surrender under real strain — no one takes his life from him.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of the crucified Christ, head bowed low in willing surrender yet his body under real strain and suffering, sinews taut, given not taken, one dominant subject, bold black ink linework, flat cel-shaded warm-grey, reverent, cinematic, dim storm sky, 1st-century
scenes.why: Guards against the victim read — 'he gave himself willingly' (John 10:18) — but willing UNDER STRAIN, not serene repose (avoids a docetic/comfortable read that erases the agony). No thorns.

scenes.concept: The risen Christ as the great high priest / Mediator — profile, wounded hands lifted toward the light of heaven, pleading, a small shadowed sinner kneeling below whom he intercedes for.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of the risen Christ as the great high priest interceding at the throne of heaven: standing in three-quarter view, both open hands lifted upward, the centre of each open palm marked by a single old HEALED scar — a thin dark closed mark lying flush and flat within the skin in the same warm skin tone, long-healed; fingers relaxed with plain natural fingertips, his bearded face lifted in earnest pleading toward a high radiant heavenly light above (the light only, no figure in it), and low behind him a single small shadowed kneeling sinner he stands between and pleads for, Christ the one dominant subject, flowing robe, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded warm gold and deep shadow, hard-edged light shaft from above, reverent, cinematic, 1st-century
macro_elements: print of the nail in the palm
scenes.why: 'Still lives to make intercession' (Heb 7:25 / Rom 8:34, at the right hand maketh intercession) — shows the MEDIATION (Christ standing between the sinner and heaven), distinct from the frontal mercy-hand of #13, not a repeated portrait. Synced to land ON the intercession word (ends 42.84). Visible nail-print (John 20:27); light stays abstract (no Father depicted).
scenes.reuse: new (risen_interceding_christ — replaced the 06c reuse per user, richer mediator composition)

scenes.concept: The land under three hours of darkness and the temple veil torn from top to bottom — his death opens the way.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of a great heavy temple veil torn from top to bottom down its middle under a sky of deep darkness, the rent opening into a shadowed empty holy place beyond, only the torn way opened, one dominant subject, bold black ink, flat cel-shaded near-monochrome dark palette, reverent, awe, 1st-century
scenes.why: REPLACES the earlier 'shaft of light' which contradicted Luke 23:45 (the sun was DARKENED) and softened the wrath-bearing. The torn veil (same verse) carries 'Christ died for us' + access opened by his death — restoring penal-substitution weight. Darkness stays dark; resurrection light lives in 11/13.

scenes.concept: The risen Christ, the nail-printed hand extended toward the viewer — that mercy held out now, come and receive it.
scenes.prompt_seed: inked biblical graphic-novel of the risen Christ facing forward, one open hand bearing the clear dark print of the nail extended warmly toward the viewer, gentle inviting gaze, warm light behind him (hard-edged, not a soft bloom), one dominant subject, bold black ink linework, flat cel-shaded gold and amber, reverent, cinematic, negative space for closing caption
scenes.why: The mandated risen-Christ mercy LANDING — the hand held out fulfills 'come, and receive it by faith' and closes on the living Christ. Synced to the full CTA window. 'Warm light' not 'glowing'.

variety_report.redteam: doctrine REVISE + craft REVISE (2026-07-01); all flags folded into v2.1: darkness->torn-veil, executioner culpable, Ps22:7 mockery, willing-under-strain, timeline re-synced, cross established by scene 2, thorns dropped, glow->warm-light, new depth stills render without Christ ref
